rule: PR opens only on a commit every configured gate held on
description: P3 coupling. `plugin/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements) is the single home of the gate end commit rule: a gate holds only for the commit its step ended on, the PR opens only on a commit every configured gate held on, on every path, a commit made after a gate sends the run back through every gate that ended on an earlier commit, and going back through the gates is bounded, with the run stopping before the PR at the bound. The source pin is ONE span carrying the whole paragraph, because each of its five sentences carries part of the claim: the condition (a gate holds only for the commit its step ended on), the gate set (validation, the version bump, and local review when it ran), the obligation and its reach (the PR opens only on a commit every configured gate held on, on every path: the workflow script, the state machine, and any step taken outside both), the rerun obligation (a later commit sends the run back through every gate that ended on an earlier commit before the PR opens), and the bound (going back through the gates is bounded, and at the bound the run stops before the PR opens). Rewriting the hold onto a commit other than the one the step ended on, dropping a gate from the set, dropping `configured`, narrowing `on every path` or one of the three paths it names, deleting the send-back obligation, or deleting the bound or the stop before the PR turns the suite red. Two consumers in `plugin/skills/open-plan-pr/SKILL.md` pin the pointers to the canonical section, a Before checklist item and a Do Not bullet, each naming `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements). One consumer in `plugin/skills/gate-check/SKILL.md` pins the Pointers bullet that names the canonical section as the gate rule the engine applies. One consumer in `plugin/workflows/standard-delivery.json` pins the pointer in the `gate_check` description, and one in `plugin/agents/overlord.md` pins the pointer that ends the "Record each gate's end commit." paragraph, together with the `expect_commit` sentence it follows. Consumers pin the reference, not the rule. Deleting a pointer or retargeting its file or section turns the suite red. What these pins honestly guarantee is exactly that these six word sequences exist in these five named files; they claim nothing about meaning and nothing about what the workflow script, the state machine, the gate-check engine, or an agent actually does. Residuals, stated plainly: (1) a meaning inversion around the pinned bytes, such as a later sentence in the section that exempts a gate or a path, is invisible; (2) agreement between this statement, the `gate_check` transitions and the script's gate loop is not checked here, because a presence pin cannot compare a statement with a routing table; (3) the Do Not bullet's negation comes from the `## Do Not` heading, not from the pinned sentence, and the heading is unpinned; (4) how the outcome is derived is unpinned here: the gate order, holding transitions and rerun bound in the gate-check contract `plugin/skills/gate-check/scripts/gate-contract.json`, the engine `plugin/skills/gate-check/scripts/gate-check.sh`, and the engine-written top-level `head` that `hivemind:record-state-result` stamps on every event, which the run ledger convention names as each gate's end commit; those are held by the workflow-script tests, not by this fixture; (5) a NEW PR-opening path, or a NEW state that makes a commit, that never carries a pointer to the canonical section is an absence defect no fixture in this directory can see, per rule 7 of the pin-authoring contract.

source.pattern: Gate end commit: a gate holds only for the commit its step ended on. The gates are validation, the version bump, and local review when it ran. The PR opens only on a commit every configured gate held on, on every path: the workflow script, the state machine, and any step taken outside both. A commit made after a gate, such as a validation fix, a bump commit, or a local review fix, sends the run back through every gate that ended on an earlier commit before the PR opens. Going back through the gates is bounded: at the bound the run stops before the PR opens.

consumers.pattern: - [ ] Every configured gate held on the commit HEAD is on, per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
- open PR on a commit a configured gate did not hold on per `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements)
A gate holds only for the commit its step ended on, per ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md (PR Requirements).

At `open_pr` it passes `expect_commit` to `hivemind:open-plan-pr` as the HEAD `gate_check` found every configured gate held on. The gate rule is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/governance/workflow.md` (PR Requirements); this paragraph does not restate it.
